title: Reading from std::cin (slide 25)
tryThis: Delete the newline after `12` in the stdin box and run again: **nothing is printed!** Reading `12` hit the end of input, which sets `eofbit`, so `good()` is false even though `n` was read correctly.
Replace the test by `if (std::cin >> n)` (or `!std::cin.fail()`): it checks only that the *read* succeeded, and is the idiomatic form.
Change the stdin to `abc`: now the read itself fails.
Try `100000`: the square overflows `int`. Run with **ASan + UBSan** to get it reported.
